question: To operate a full-sized school bus in Massachusetts, what CDL endorsements must you hold?
choice_a: A Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement and a School Bus (S) endorsement
choice_b: A Passenger (P) endorsement and a School Bus (S) endorsement
choice_c: A School Bus (S) endorsement only
choice_d: A Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement and a Passenger (P) endorsement
explanation: The manual states that to operate a full-sized school bus in Massachusetts, you must have a CDL with a Passenger (P) endorsement and a School Bus (S) endorsement, in addition to a School Bus Driver Certificate from the Department of Public Utilities.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Preface, School Bus Requirements

question: In addition to the required CDL endorsements, what else must a full-sized school bus driver obtain in Massachusetts?
choice_a: No additional document is required beyond the CDL endorsements
choice_b: A commercial insurance rider from the RMV
choice_c: A Motor Bus Driver Certificate from the RMV
choice_d: A School Bus Driver Certificate from the Department of Public Utilities
explanation: The manual states that to operate a full-sized school bus, you also need a School Bus Driver Certificate from the Department of Public Utilities.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Preface, School Bus Requirements

question: What is required to operate a restricted school bus (maximum seating capacity of fourteen passengers) in Massachusetts?
choice_a: A Class A CDL with an air brakes endorsement only
choice_b: A Class D (Passenger Vehicle) license and a "Restricted School Bus Driver" certificate from the Department of Public Utilities
choice_c: A learner's permit with adult supervision
choice_d: A full CDL with Passenger and School Bus endorsements
explanation: The manual specifies that to operate a restricted school bus (max seating capacity of fourteen passengers), you need a Class D (Passenger Vehicle) license and a "Restricted School Bus Driver" certificate from the Department of Public Utilities.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Preface, School Bus Requirements

question: If you will operate a school bus with air brakes in Massachusetts, what additional requirement applies?
choice_a: No additional testing is required beyond the standard school bus certification
choice_b: You must complete an additional 10 hours of behind-the-wheel training
choice_c: You must pass an air-brakes written exam at the RMV and pass an air-brakes road test
choice_d: You must obtain a separate air brakes certificate from the Department of Public Utilities
explanation: The manual notes that to operate a school bus with air brakes, you must, in addition, pass an air-brakes written exam at the RMV and pass an air-brakes road test.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Preface, School Bus Requirements

question: How many continuous years of driving experience must you have to qualify for a full-sized or restricted School Bus Certificate in Massachusetts?
choice_a: Five (5) continuous years
choice_b: Three (3) continuous years
choice_c: One (1) continuous year
choice_d: Two (2) continuous years
explanation: The eligibility requirements state you must have three (3) continuous years of driving experience to qualify for a full-sized or restricted School Bus Certificate.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Preface, School Bus Driver Eligibility Requirements

question: Which background checks must a Massachusetts school bus driver applicant pass, according to the eligibility requirements?
choice_a: A federal security clearance check
choice_b: An employer reference check only
choice_c: A Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) check and a Sex Offender Record Information (SORI) check
choice_d: A credit history check only
explanation: The eligibility requirements include passing a Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) check and a Sex Offender Record Information (SORI) check, in addition to a DOT physical exam and other requirements.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Preface, School Bus Driver Eligibility Requirements

question: Under the Basic First Aid Training for School Bus Drivers Law, how long does the first aid course typically last and what specific skill must it cover?
choice_a: Four hours, including defibrillator use
choice_b: Eight hours, including CPR certification
choice_c: One hour, covering only bandaging techniques
choice_d: Two hours, including training on administering an epinephrine auto-injector
explanation: The manual states the first aid course shall typically be two hours and shall include training relative to the administration of an epinephrine auto-injector.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Preface, Basic First Aid Training for School Bus Drivers

question: For which type of vehicle operator is the Basic First Aid Training for School Bus Drivers NOT a requirement?
choice_a: Restricted school bus operators
choice_b: Full-sized school bus operators
choice_c: 7D vehicle operators
choice_d: All operators must complete it regardless of vehicle type
explanation: The manual explicitly states that this first aid course is not a requirement for 7D vehicle operators.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Preface, Basic First Aid Training for School Bus Drivers

question: How is the "danger zone" around a school bus defined?
choice_a: Only the area directly behind the rear bumper of the bus
choice_b: Only the area on the driver's side of the bus
choice_c: The interior aisle of the bus where students walk
choice_d: The area on all sides of the bus where children are in the most danger of being hit by another vehicle or their own bus
explanation: Section 10.1.1 defines the danger zone as the area on all sides of the bus where children are in the most danger of being hit, either by another vehicle or their own bus.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: How far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus, and which portion is the most dangerous?
choice_a: As much as 50 feet, with the middle 20 feet being the most dangerous
choice_b: As much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous
choice_c: As much as 100 feet, with the last 10 feet being the most dangerous
choice_d: Exactly 10 feet, with no portion more dangerous than another
explanation: The manual states the danger zone may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: Why is the area to the left of a school bus always considered part of the danger zone?
choice_a: Because students always exit on the left side
choice_b: Because of passing cars
choice_c: Because the driver's mirrors cannot reach that side at all
choice_d: Because the fuel tank is located on the left side
explanation: The manual states that the area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: When properly adjusted, what should the outside left and right side flat mirrors allow you to see?
choice_a: The front bumper danger zone only
choice_b: Oncoming traffic in the opposite lane only
choice_c: 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus, along the sides of the bus, and the rear tires touching the ground
choice_d: Only the interior of the bus
explanation: Section 10.1.3 states the outside flat mirrors should be adjusted so you can see 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus, along the sides of the bus, and the rear tires touching the ground.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.3 Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: How far behind a school bus can the blind spot extend, depending on the length and width of the bus?
choice_a: It never extends beyond the rear bumper
choice_b: Up to 50 feet
choice_c: Up to 1,000 feet
choice_d: Up to 400 feet
explanation: The manual states the blind spot behind the bus extends 50 to 150 feet and could extend up to 400 feet depending on the length and width of the bus.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.3 Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: What is a key limitation of the outside left and right side convex mirrors on a school bus?
choice_a: They present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance from the bus
choice_b: They cannot be adjusted by the driver
choice_c: They only function at night
choice_d: They show only the interior of the bus
explanation: The manual explains that convex mirrors present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance from the bus, so the driver must ensure they are properly adjusted.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: When properly positioned, the outside convex mirrors should allow you to see at least how much traffic on either side of the bus?
choice_a: At least one traffic lane on either side of the bus
choice_b: At least three traffic lanes on either side of the bus
choice_c: Only the lane the bus is traveling in
choice_d: The entire width of the roadway regardless of number of lanes
explanation: Section 10.1.4 states you should position the convex mirrors to see at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus, along with the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts and the front of the rear tires touching the ground.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.4 Outside Left and Right Side Convex Mirrors

question: What is the purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors on a school bus?
choice_a: To see only oncoming traffic in the opposite lane
choice_b: To replace the need for the overhead rearview mirror
choice_c: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
choice_d: To see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision
explanation: Section 10.1.5 states the crossover mirrors are used to see the front bumper "danger zone" area directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision, and to view the danger zone areas to the left and right sides, including the service door and front wheel area.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.5 Outside Left and Right Side Crossover Mirrors

question: What is the primary purpose of the overhead inside rearview mirror mounted above the windshield on a school bus?
choice_a: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
choice_b: To view traffic approaching from the front of the bus
choice_c: To replace the outside convex mirrors
choice_d: To check tire pressure on the rear axle
explanation: Section 10.1.6 states this mirror is mounted directly above the windshield on the driver's side and is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.1.6 Overhead Inside Rearview Mirror

question: According to the manual, when are more students killed relative to school bus travel?
choice_a: Student fatalities related to school buses are extremely rare in all situations
choice_b: Fatalities are equally distributed between loading, unloading, and riding inside the bus
choice_c: More students are killed as passengers inside the bus than while loading or unloading
choice_d: More students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside a school bus
explanation: Section 10.2 states that more students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside of a school bus, which is why loading and unloading procedures are so critical.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2 Loading and Unloading

question: When approaching a school bus stop, when should you activate the alternating flashing amber warning lights (if so equipped)?
choice_a: At least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law
choice_b: Exactly 500 feet before the stop, with no time equivalent given
choice_c: At least 1,000 feet before the stop
choice_d: Only after the bus has come to a complete stop
explanation: Section 10.2.1 instructs drivers to activate alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: When approaching a school bus stop, when should the right turn signal indicator be turned on?
choice_a: There is no guidance on turn signal timing in the manual
choice_b: About 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over
choice_c: Only after the door has already opened
choice_d: About 1,000 feet before pulling over
explanation: The manual states to turn on the right turn signal indicator about 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: When stopping for students, how far away from the students at the designated stop should the front bumper of the school bus be, and why?
choice_a: There is no specified distance; the driver should stop as close as possible
choice_b: At least 50 feet away, to allow room for other vehicles to pass
choice_c: Exactly 2 feet away, to minimize walking distance for students
choice_d: At least 10 feet away, which forces the students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements
explanation: The manual instructs bringing the school bus to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students at the designated stop, forcing students to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: Why should the dome light be on while loading students in the dark?
choice_a: It automatically activates the alternating red lights
choice_b: It has no connection to loading procedures and is only for post-trip inspections
choice_c: It is part of the recommended loading procedure to help see and be seen while boarding
choice_d: It is legally required only for buses without headlights
explanation: Section 10.2.2 states that students should board slowly, in single file, using the handrail, and the dome light should be on while loading in the dark.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: If you cannot account for a student outside the bus during loading, what should you do?
choice_a: Secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus
choice_b: Leave the bus unattended to search the surrounding area
choice_c: Immediately drive away and report it to the school afterward
choice_d: Sound the horn repeatedly until the student appears
explanation: The manual instructs that if you cannot account for a student outside the bus during loading, you should secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: When students are loading at the school campus, what should the driver do in addition to the general loading procedures?
choice_a: Turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment
choice_b: Activate the stop signal arm even though the bus is parked at school
choice_c: Leave the engine running at all times with the key in the ignition
choice_d: Disable the dome light to conserve battery power
explanation: The manual states that when loading at the school campus, the driver should turn off the ignition switch and remove the key if leaving the driver's compartment.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.2 Loading Procedures

question: When unloading students along the route, how far should students walk from the side of the bus before the driver pulls away?
choice_a: At least 10 feet away, to a position where the driver can plainly see all students
choice_b: Exactly 2 feet away
choice_c: At least 50 feet away
choice_d: Students do not need to move away from the bus
explanation: Section 10.2.3 instructs the driver to tell students to exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When a student must cross the roadway after exiting the bus, how far in front of the right corner of the bumper should they walk before stopping?
choice_a: There is no specified distance for this step
choice_b: At least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, while remaining away from the front of the bus
choice_c: Directly at the front bumper, touching it
choice_d: At least 50 feet in front of the bumper
explanation: The manual states students should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, but still remaining away from the front of the school bus, before stopping at the edge of the roadway.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: Before crossing the roadway, what should a student do after reaching the edge of the roadway?
choice_a: Cross immediately without stopping
choice_b: Run across as quickly as possible
choice_c: Stop and look in all directions, check that the bus's red flashing lights are still flashing, and wait for the driver's signal
choice_d: Wait for another student to cross first, regardless of the driver's signal
explanation: The manual instructs that when students reach the edge of the roadway, they should stop and look in all directions to make sure the roadway is clear, check that the red flashing lights on the bus are still flashing, and wait for the driver's signal before crossing.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: If you have missed a student's unloading stop, what should you do?
choice_a: Immediately back up to the correct stop
choice_b: Do not back up; be sure to follow local procedures
choice_c: Radio the student's parents before taking any action
choice_d: Continue the route and address it only at the end of the day
explanation: The manual gives a specific note: if you have missed a student's unloading stop, do not back up, and be sure to follow local procedures.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When unloading students at school, what should the driver do while walking through the bus?
choice_a: Only check the fuel gauge
choice_b: Check for hiding/sleeping students and items left by students
choice_c: Nothing; walking through the bus is not part of the unloading procedure
choice_d: Collect all students' backpacks for inspection
explanation: Section 10.2.4 instructs the driver to walk through the bus and check for hiding/sleeping students and items left by students when unloading at school.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.4 Unloading Procedures at School

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What should students be told to do if they drop an object near the bus during loading or unloading?
choice_a: Return for it after school ends
choice_b: Immediately pick it up before continuing to board or exit
choice_c: Leave the dropped object, move to a point of safety out of the danger zones, and try to get the driver's attention to retrieve it
choice_d: Ask another student to retrieve it while they wait at the danger zone boundary
explanation: The manual warns that stopping or returning to pick up a dropped object can cause a student to disappear from the driver's sight at a dangerous moment, so students should leave the object, move to a point of safety, and try to get the driver's attention to retrieve it.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.5 Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

topic: Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading
question: What hazard is described under "Handrail Hang-ups" in the manual?
choice_a: Students have been injured or killed when clothing, accessories, or body parts get caught in the handrail or door as they exit the bus
choice_b: Handrails are electrically charged in older buses
choice_c: Handrails obstruct the driver's view of the mirrors
choice_d: Handrails frequently break under normal use, causing falls
explanation: The manual describes handrail hang-ups as a special danger where students have been injured or killed when clothing, accessories, or parts of their body get caught in the handrail or door as they exit the bus.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.5 Special Dangers of Loading and Unloading

question: During a post-trip inspection, what school-bus-specific items should you pay special attention to for mechanical or operational problems?
choice_a: The passenger seat upholstery
choice_b: The radio and entertainment system only
choice_c: Mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms
choice_d: The fuel cap color coding
explanation: Section 10.2.6 states that during the post-trip walk-through, you should look for mechanical/operational problems with special attention to items unique to school buses, such as mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.6 Post-trip Inspection

question: If you find damage, vandalism, or a mechanical problem during a post-trip inspection, what should you do?
choice_a: Ignore it unless a student was injured
choice_b: Repair it yourself before the next route
choice_c: Note it in a personal log and address it the following week
choice_d: Report it immediately to your supervisor or school authorities
explanation: The manual states that any problems or special situations found during the post-trip inspection should be reported immediately to your supervisor or school authorities.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.2.6 Post-trip Inspection

question: What is described as the first and most important consideration in deciding whether to evacuate a school bus?
choice_a: Contacting the students' parents
choice_b: Waiting for police to arrive before taking any action
choice_c: Determining which door is closest to the driver
choice_d: Recognizing the hazard
explanation: Section 10.3.1 states that the first and most important consideration is for the driver to recognize the hazard, and if time permits, to contact the dispatcher before deciding to evacuate.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: As a general rule, how is student safety and control best maintained during an emergency or impending crisis?
choice_a: By always evacuating immediately regardless of the situation
choice_b: By keeping students on the bus, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury
choice_c: By having students leave through whichever exit is nearest, without direction
choice_d: By instructing students to call their parents for guidance
explanation: The manual states that as a general rule, student safety and control is best maintained by keeping students on the bus during an emergency, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury, and that the decision to evacuate must be a timely one.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: Which of the following is listed as a condition requiring a mandatory evacuation of a school bus?
choice_a: The bus is running five minutes behind schedule
choice_b: The bus is on fire or there is a threat of a fire
choice_c: The heater in the bus is not functioning
choice_d: A student requests to be let off early
explanation: The manual lists several mandatory evacuation conditions, including that the bus is on fire or there is a threat of a fire.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies, Mandatory Evacuations

question: According to the manual, a bus stalled in which location requires a mandatory evacuation?
choice_a: On a bridge with no other traffic present
choice_b: In a school parking lot
choice_c: On or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_d: At a designated bus stop
explanation: The manual specifies that the driver must evacuate the bus when it is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies, Mandatory Evacuations

question: How far off the road, and in what direction, should a "safe place" for evacuated students generally be located?
choice_a: At least 1,000 feet off the road in the direction away from oncoming traffic
choice_b: At least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic
choice_c: Directly behind the bus, regardless of distance
choice_d: At least 10 feet off the road in any direction
explanation: Section 10.3.2 states that a safe place will be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, which keeps students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials during an evacuation, how far upwind should students be led?
choice_a: No specific distance is needed as long as they are off the bus
choice_b: At least 50 feet
choice_c: At least 1,000 feet
choice_d: At least 300 feet
explanation: The manual states that students should be led upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If the bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado and evacuation is ordered, what should the driver direct students to do if no building shelter is readily available?
choice_a: Escort them to a nearby ditch or culvert and direct them to lie face down with hands covering their head
choice_b: Have them remain seated on the bus with seatbelts fastened
choice_c: Direct them to run individually in different directions
choice_d: Have them stand together next to the bus for protection
explanation: The manual instructs that if the bus is in the direct path of a sighted tornado, students should be escorted to a nearby ditch or culvert if shelter in a building is not readily available, and directed to lie face down with hands covering their head, far enough away that the bus cannot topple on them.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: Before evacuating students, what should the driver do to secure the bus?
choice_a: Turn off the hazard-warning lights to conserve the battery
choice_b: Leave the transmission in gear to prevent rolling
choice_c: Leave the engine running to keep the interior lights on
choice_d: Place the transmission in Park or Neutral, set the parking brakes, shut off the engine, remove the ignition key, and activate hazard-warning lights
explanation: The manual's general evacuation procedures instruct the driver to secure the bus by placing the transmission in Park or Neutral, setting the parking brakes, shutting off the engine, removing the ignition key, and activating hazard-warning lights.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: According to the manual, when should you move a student you believe may have suffered a neck or spinal injury during an evacuation?
choice_a: Immediately, regardless of the type of injury
choice_b: Only after emergency responders give explicit permission by radio
choice_c: Never, under any circumstances
choice_d: Only unless his or her life is in immediate danger
explanation: The manual instructs: do not move a student you believe may have suffered a neck or spinal injury unless his or her life is in immediate danger, and that special procedures must be used to move such victims to prevent further injury.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If the radio is inoperable during an emergency and no passing motorist or area resident is available, what does the manual describe as the last resort for calling for help?
choice_a: Sending a single unaccompanied young student for help
choice_b: Having the driver leave the bus and all students to find a phone
choice_c: Waiting indefinitely for someone to notice the bus
choice_d: Dispatching two older, responsible students to go for help
explanation: The manual states that if there is no radio, or the radio is inoperable, the driver should dispatch a passing motorist or area resident to call for help, and as a last resort, dispatch two older, responsible students to go for help.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: What characterizes a "passive" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: It always has gates and flashing red lights
choice_b: It is monitored remotely by the railroad company at all times
choice_c: It does not have any type of traffic control device, and the decision to proceed rests entirely in the driver's hands
choice_d: It is only found on private roads
explanation: Section 10.4.1 describes a passive crossing as one without any type of traffic control device, requiring the driver to recognize the crossing, search for any train, and decide if there is sufficient clear space to cross safely, with the decision to proceed resting entirely in the driver's hands.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: What defines an "active" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: It has a traffic control device installed to regulate traffic, such as flashing red lights, with or without bells, or gates
choice_b: It is used only by freight trains, never passenger trains
choice_c: It has no signs or markings of any kind
choice_d: It requires a police officer to be present at all times
explanation: The manual states that an active crossing has a traffic control device installed to regulate traffic, including flashing red lights with or without bells, and flashing red lights with bells and gates.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: What does the round, black-on-yellow advance warning sign placed ahead of a railroad-highway crossing tell you to do?
choice_a: Speed up to clear the crossing before a train arrives
choice_b: Slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming
choice_c: Stop only if you hear a train whistle
choice_d: Change lanes immediately
explanation: Section 10.4.2 explains that the round, black-on-yellow advance warning sign tells you to slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: At a railroad crossing with a cross-buck sign but no white stop line painted on the pavement, where must you stop the bus?
choice_a: Directly on the tracks for the best view
choice_b: At least 500 feet before the sign
choice_c: You are not required to stop if there is no painted line
choice_d: Before the cross-buck sign
explanation: The manual states that if there is no white line painted on the pavement, you must stop the bus before the cross-buck sign, which requires you to yield the right-of-way to the train.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: If the gate at a railroad crossing stays down after the train has passed, what should you do?
choice_a: Honk the horn until the gate rises automatically
choice_b: Wait exactly five minutes and then proceed regardless of the gate
choice_c: Do not drive around the gate; instead, call your dispatcher
choice_d: Drive around the gate carefully since the train has already passed
explanation: The manual instructs that if the gate stays down after the train passes, you should not drive around the gate, but instead call your dispatcher.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.2 Warning Signs and Devices

question: When approaching a railroad-highway crossing, at approximately what distance before the crossing should you activate your hazard lights?
choice_a: Approximately 200 feet before the crossing
choice_b: Approximately 20 feet before the crossing
choice_c: Hazard lights should not be used when approaching a railroad crossing
choice_d: Approximately 1 mile before the crossing
explanation: Section 10.4.3 recommends activating hazard lights approximately 200 feet before the crossing to make sure your intentions are known.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: At a railroad crossing, how close and how far should you stop from the nearest rail?
choice_a: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail
choice_b: Exactly at the cross-buck sign, regardless of distance to the rail
choice_c: No closer than 5 feet and no farther than 10 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: No closer than 100 feet and no farther than 200 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual instructs stopping no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where you have the best view of the tracks.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: While stopped at a railroad crossing, what should you do besides setting the brakes?
choice_a: Turn up the radio so you can hear a train whistle over engine noise
choice_b: Close all windows and doors to keep noise out
choice_c: Allow students to move around freely to look out different windows
choice_d: Turn off all radios and noisy equipment, silence the passengers, and open the service door and driver's window to look and listen for an approaching train
explanation: The manual instructs that at the crossing you should turn off all radios and noisy equipment, silence the passengers, and open the service door and driver's window to look and listen for an approaching train.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: At a multiple-track crossing, where should you stop before proceeding?
choice_a: There is no need to stop at multiple-track crossings if the first track is clear
choice_b: In the middle of the tracks to check for trains from both directions
choice_c: Before each individual set of tracks, stopping and restarting repeatedly
choice_d: Only before the first set of tracks; once sure no train is approaching on any track, proceed across all tracks until completely clear
explanation: The manual instructs that at a multiple-track crossing, you should stop only before the first set of tracks, and when sure no train is approaching on any track, proceed across all of the tracks until you have completely cleared them.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: If the gate comes down after you have already started crossing the tracks, what should you do?
choice_a: Back up off the tracks to avoid damaging the gate
choice_b: Stop immediately on the tracks and wait for the gate to rise
choice_c: Drive through it even if it means you will break the gate
choice_d: Honk your horn and wait for a railroad worker to raise the gate
explanation: The manual instructs that if the gate comes down after you have started across, you should drive through it even if it means you will break the gate, since stopping on the tracks is far more dangerous.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: If your school bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, what should you direct everyone to do?
choice_a: Get everyone out and off the tracks immediately, moving away at an angle that is both away from the tracks and toward the train
choice_b: Stay on the bus and wait for help to arrive
choice_c: Push the bus off the tracks before evacuating
choice_d: Move away from the tracks in the same direction the train is traveling, away from an oncoming train
explanation: Section 10.4.4 instructs that if the bus stalls or is trapped on the tracks, everyone should get out and off the tracks immediately, moving away at an angle both away from the tracks and toward the train.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: As a general rule, how much should you add to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area beyond a railroad crossing?
choice_a: No additional length is necessary
choice_b: 100 feet
choice_c: 50 feet
choice_d: 15 feet
explanation: The manual states that as a general rule, you should add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area on the other side of a crossing.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: The manual warns that you should be especially careful at which type of crossing, even if active signals indicate the tracks are clear?
choice_a: Passive crossings
choice_b: Crossings with a police officer present
choice_c: Crossings with gates
choice_d: Crossings inside a school parking lot
explanation: The manual states that passive crossings are those without any type of traffic control device, and you must be especially careful at them; even if there are active railroad signals indicating the tracks are clear, you must still look and listen to be sure it is safe to proceed.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.4.4 Special Situations

question: Why does the manual advise against dealing with on-bus behavior problems while loading and unloading students?
choice_a: Behavior problems are not the driver's responsibility at any time
choice_b: It is only a concern for restricted school buses, not full-sized ones
choice_c: Loading and unloading requires all of the driver's concentration, so the driver should not take their eyes off what is happening outside the bus
choice_d: Students are legally permitted to misbehave during loading and unloading
explanation: Section 10.5.1 explains that loading and unloading requires all of the driver's concentration, and the driver should not take their eyes off what is happening outside the bus; if there is a behavior problem, the driver should wait until unloading students are safely off and away, pulling over if necessary.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.5.1 Don't Deal with On-bus Problems When Loading and Unloading

question: According to the manual, where is a driver permitted to put a student off the bus for a behavior problem?
choice_a: Only at the nearest police station
choice_b: Anywhere the driver deems appropriate along the route
choice_c: Only at school or at his or her designated school bus stop
choice_d: Students can never be put off the bus under any circumstances, even at school
explanation: Section 10.5.2 states that a driver should never put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop; if the offense is serious enough, the driver should call for a school administrator or the police.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: When addressing a student causing a serious problem on the bus, what demeanor does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Ignore the student entirely until arriving at school
choice_b: Yell loudly to assert authority immediately
choice_c: Speak respectfully and courteously with a firm voice, reminding the offender of expected behavior without showing anger
choice_d: Threaten to remove the student from school entirely
explanation: The manual advises standing up and speaking respectfully to the offender in a courteous manner with a firm voice, reminding them of expected behavior, without showing anger, while still showing that you mean business.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.5.2 Handling Serious Problems

question: According to the manual, the Department of Transportation requires antilock braking systems on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after which date?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1995
choice_c: January 1, 2000
choice_d: March 1, 1999
explanation: Section 10.6.1 states that the DOT requires ABS on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: For hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 lbs or more, when does the ABS requirement apply?
choice_a: Vehicles built on or after March 1, 1998
choice_b: All hydraulically braked vehicles, regardless of build date
choice_c: Vehicles built on or after January 1, 2005
choice_d: Vehicles built on or after March 1, 1999
explanation: The manual states that hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after March 1, 1999 are required to have ABS.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: What is the main benefit of ABS according to the manual?
choice_a: It guarantees a shorter stopping distance in every situation
choice_b: It allows you to safely follow other vehicles more closely
choice_c: It helps you avoid wheel lock-up and maintain control, allowing you to steer around an obstacle while braking
choice_d: It eliminates the need for regular brake maintenance
explanation: Section 10.6.2 explains that ABS helps you avoid wheel lock-up and maintain control; you may or may not stop faster with ABS, but you should be able to steer around an obstacle while braking and avoid skids caused by over-braking.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.2 How ABS Helps You

question: In an emergency braking situation on a bus equipped with ABS, what should you NOT do?
choice_a: Pump the brakes
choice_b: Attempt to steer around an obstacle
choice_c: Apply steady pressure to the brake pedal
choice_d: Monitor the bus and back off the brakes if it is safe to do so
explanation: Section 10.6.3 states that you should brake the same way regardless of whether you have ABS, but in emergency braking, you should not pump the brakes on a bus with ABS.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.3 Braking with ABS

question: On newer vehicles, what should the yellow ABS malfunction lamp normally do when the vehicle starts up?
choice_a: Stay on permanently as a reminder that ABS is installed
choice_b: Remain off at all times unless there is a malfunction
choice_c: Flash continuously until the vehicle exceeds highway speed
choice_d: Come on for a bulb check and then go out quickly
explanation: Section 10.6.4 states that as a system check on newer vehicles, the malfunction lamp comes on at start-up for a bulb check and then goes out quickly; on older systems, the lamp could stay on until you are driving over five mph.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.4 Braking if ABS is Not Working

question: If your ABS malfunctions, what does the manual say you should do?
choice_a: Disconnect the brake system entirely until repairs are made
choice_b: Continue driving without regard for brake performance since ABS is only a minor feature
choice_c: Stop driving the bus immediately and permanently
choice_d: Drive normally, since you still have regular brakes, but get the system serviced soon
explanation: The manual states that if your ABS malfunctions, you still have regular brakes, so you should drive normally but get the system serviced soon.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.4 Braking if ABS is Not Working

question: Which of the following is TRUE about ABS, according to the manual's safety reminders?
choice_a: ABS will prevent skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_b: ABS will not allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully
choice_c: ABS will compensate for bad brakes or poor brake maintenance
choice_d: ABS will always shorten your stopping distance
explanation: Section 10.6.5 lists several safety reminders, including that ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully; it also won't necessarily shorten stopping distance, won't prevent power or turning skids, and won't compensate for bad brakes or poor maintenance.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.6.5 Safety Reminders

question: According to the manual, when should the roof-mounted white strobe light on a school bus (if equipped) be used?
choice_a: Only when transporting students on a field trip
choice_b: Only during scheduled maintenance checks
choice_c: When you have limited visibility, meaning you cannot easily see around the bus
choice_d: Continuously, at all times the bus is in operation
explanation: Section 10.7.1 states that the overhead strobe light should be used when you have limited visibility, meaning you cannot easily see around you in front, behind, or beside the school bus, subject to state or local regulations.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.1 Strobe Lights

question: How does the manual describe the effect of strong winds on a school bus?
choice_a: Wind only affects buses traveling at low speeds
choice_b: The side of a school bus acts like a sail on a sailboat, and strong winds can push the bus sideways or even off the road or tip it over
choice_c: School buses are unaffected by wind due to their weight
choice_d: Wind primarily affects the bus's braking system, not its steering
explanation: Section 10.7.2 states that the side of a school bus acts like a sail on a sailboat, and strong winds can push the bus sideways, move it off the road, or in extreme conditions, tip it over.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.2 Driving in High Winds

question: According to the manual, when should you never back a school bus?
choice_a: When backing at a designated student pick-up point
choice_b: When a lookout is posted
choice_c: When students are outside of the bus
choice_d: When the parking brake is set
explanation: Section 10.7.3 states that backing a school bus is strongly discouraged and that you should never back a school bus when students are outside of the bus, since backing is dangerous and increases the risk of a collision.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing

question: What is the purpose of posting a lookout when backing a school bus, and what should the lookout NOT do?
choice_a: The lookout should give precise steering directions to the driver at all times
choice_b: The lookout warns of obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles, but should not give directions on how to back the bus
choice_c: The lookout's only job is to operate the bus's hazard lights
choice_d: The lookout should stand directly behind the bus in its path
explanation: The manual states the purpose of the lookout is to warn the driver about obstacles, approaching persons, and other vehicles, and that the lookout should not give directions on how to back the bus.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing

question: If no lookout is available and you must back the bus, what should you do before backing?
choice_a: Proceed slowly without any additional precautions
choice_b: Rely solely on the interior overhead mirror to check behind the bus
choice_c: Set the parking brake, turn off the motor, take the keys with you, and walk to the rear of the bus to determine whether the way is clear
choice_d: Have a student stand behind the bus to guide you
explanation: The manual instructs that if no lookout is available, you should set the parking brake, turn off the motor, take the keys with you, and walk to the rear of the bus to determine whether the way is clear.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.3 Backing

question: How much tail swing can a school bus have, and what should you do to account for it?
choice_a: Up to a one-foot tail swing, which requires no special mirror checks
choice_b: School buses have no tail swing due to their rigid frame design
choice_c: Up to a three-foot tail swing; you need to check your mirrors before and during any turning movements
choice_d: Up to a ten-foot tail swing; tail swing only matters when driving in reverse
explanation: Section 10.7.4 states that a school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, and you need to check your mirrors before and during any turning movements to monitor the tail swing.
source_note: Massachusetts Commercial Driver's License Manual (Modernized Testing System, base AAMVA content Version: July 2017, Massachusetts-specific front matter revised March 2025), Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) -- Section 10, School Buses, 10.7.4 Tail Swing
